summary: Verified by construction that only baselines/review.txt line 29 moved since the round-4 reviewed tree: `git diff-tree -r --name-status 2cdc387d884f8033d6d412d4a4799faf5041323c $(git write-tree)` prints one path, and a line diff of that file prints one hunk, 29c29. Every factual claim in the rewritten line checks out against the tree. Round 2 is diff b381c73c with staged_tree 469567ea8610c313b06a655a5661a606fec5fe36 and BOTH roles changes-requested on 0036 (reviewer F5, test-reviewer M0.79-T5); `git ls-tree -r 469567ea8610 -- docs/internal/product/decisions/` ends at 0036 while the round-1 (73bbbb56), round-3 (b1885741) and round-4 (2cdc387d) trees all end at 0035, so exactly one reviewed hash carried the sweep and round 3 was the re-review after removal. .harness/review/77b8605b69d17e03....gates exists with no .reviewer.json and no .test-reviewer.json beside it and no p079 packet, gated at 07:19:34, thirteen seconds before the round-3 hash was gated at 07:19:47: the second sweep is recorded as self-caught and the tree agrees. F10's attribution is accurate and does not understate either, since the same sentence still says both roles blocked. cost.md claim re-verified by RUNNING the selector: `printf 'docs/internal/product/decisions/0036-x.md\n.agents/skills/brevity/SKILL.md\n' | ./scripts/which-standards.sh` emits git.md, sdd.md, testing.md, performance.md and no cost.md, matching the standards block of p079-r2 through r5 verbatim. F12's replacement is exact: ADR-0036 line 88 reads '## Which formats change' / '**Both.**', then a Checkpoint bullet and a CommitDelta bullet; the file is 208 lines and untracked. build-index.sh globs '.agents/skills/*/' from the filesystem with no index or --cached read, so the worktree claim holds. Two minors remain, both in the same line and both about prose the F11 fix added rather than about a fact: the F11 correction was appended without deleting the sentence it corrects, and the M0.76 cross-reference points the wrong way. Neither is worth a sixth round; review.md rule minors-land carries them to the commit body, and rule minors-land's own warning -- 'the next round's surface is the prose the fix just added' -- is exactly what F13 is. No object-store request is added or changed by any of the nine files: no code moved in this commit at all. Landable.

findings.failure_scenario: The F11 fix was APPENDED and the sentence it corrects was left standing, so the entry now asserts both P and not-P. Sentence 2 still reads, byte-identical to the round-4 tree 2cdc387d I quoted in F11, 'Splitting further means committing a skill without the index row that resolves it, or an index row pointing at a file the commit does not carry.' Four sentences later: 'A SPLIT SEAM DOES EXIST and an earlier draft denied it: skill plus adapter plus index rows is self-consistent, and the review/SKILL.md paragraph plus the two briefs is self-consistent once that lands.' The second clause is right and the first is the exhaustiveness claim it refutes. Two concrete failures. (1) 'an earlier draft denied it' is itself false about the staged bytes: the denial is not in an earlier draft, it is in this line, 240 characters earlier, and a reader who trusts that phrase stops looking for it. (2) F11's scenario is only half closed -- a future author still finds a quotable sentence saying a skill-landing commit cannot be split without breaking an index row, and can cite it without the correction, because the two sit in one 3,000-character line that nobody quotes whole. The remedy is DELETION of that sentence, not another rewrite: the surviving clause already carries the true reason ('splitting at round 4 costs four fresh rounds and saves none') and the true coupling ('separating them from the M4.10b work in flight is what created this task') without it. Recording rather than blocking, per review.md rule minors-land, and because this packet's own escalation banner says the honest move on prose that keeps being wrong is to delete it rather than correct it again.

'Inflating the mechanism's catch count is the failure the M0.76 entry below records.' Wrong direction and imprecise target, in the one sentence of the entry whose subject is inaccurate attribution. Direction: rounds:M0.76 is at line 26 of the staged baselines/review.txt and rounds:M0.79 is at line 29, appended last, so NOTHING is below it -- a reader following the pointer downward off the end of the file either gives up or lands on the wrong entry, and every future rounds: line lands below M0.79 and will make 'below' resolve to something unrelated. Target: the M0.76 entry records four unmeasured or misattributed NUMBERS about a tree ('~19 files', 11,481, 120 rows, '13 of 51 to line wrapping') and a quotation attributed to a pattern in no committed object; it records nothing about the review mechanism's catch count, so the sentence claims a precedent the cited entry does not carry. 'the M0.76 entry above' fixes the direction; naming the class -- a number I had not measured -- fixes the target.
